title: Glide, Fillers, Figures, Headroom & Slots
description: Anchored grid cells that transition, last-row fillers, OpenType figures, HDR headroom on hover, and a self-reading component.

drops.title: Cells That Glide
drops.description: Anchor each tile to its own grid cell and a reflow becomes an inset change the browser can interpolate.
drops.concept: Grid tracks are layout concepts, not elements, so nothing can transition between them — which is why reordering a grid normally snaps. Giving each cell an anchor-name (scoped with anchor-scope so the name can repeat) and absolutely positioning the tile against it turns every reflow into animatable inset values. Unlike a view transition it is fully interruptible: resize mid-flight and the tiles redirect from wherever they are.
drops.source: Bramus — “Animating CSS Grid Layouts with CSS Anchor Positioning”

interaction.mouse: Shuffle and filter the grid, or drag the window edge to change the column count mid-animation.
interaction.click: Buttons reorder, filter, outline the cells and switch between the anchored technique and a FLIP fallback.
interaction.touch: Tap the controls; the duration, easing and tile-count sliders retune the motion live.

drops.title: No Ragged Last Row
drops.description: The 1px-gap border grid falls apart when the final row runs short — count the empty slots and fill them.
drops.concept: A grid with a 1px gap over a rule-coloured background draws every cell border for free, until an incomplete last row lets the container show through. The fix is arithmetic: ceil(items / cols) * cols − items, read from the resolved grid-template-columns rather than hard-coded per breakpoint. One element with grid-column: span n closes the gap without drawing rules between the blanks.
drops.source: Tim Wilson — “Filling the last row of a responsive grid”

interaction.mouse: Resize the window and watch the filler count recompute against the new column count.
interaction.click: Toggle the fillers off to see the ragged edge, tint them, or collapse them into one spanning cell.
interaction.touch: Item-count, cell-size and rule-width sliders drive the same grid.

drops.title: Figures That Hold Still
drops.description: Four OpenType switches through two CSS properties — and a live detector for whether your font has the glyphs.
drops.concept: Tabular figures give every digit the same advance width, so a live value stops shuffling sideways on each tick; old-style figures have ascenders and descenders so numbers settle into prose; diagonal fractions and real small caps finish the job. The catch is that many font builds ship without the glyphs, and the browser silently does nothing — so this demo measures the rendered width with and without each feature and tells you.
drops.source: Carmen Ansio — “Better dashboard figures with OpenType features”

interaction.mouse: Watch the two live columns — the proportional one twitches, the tabular one never moves.
interaction.click: Toggle each OpenType switch and swap the font stack; the detector dots re-run on every change.
interaction.touch: All controls are checkboxes and a select, both thumb-sized.

drops.title: Brighter Than White
drops.description: HDR screens keep headroom above page white — dynamic-range-limit hands it to one element on hover.
drops.concept: An HDR display can show colours brighter than the page's white, and CSS now decides who may spend that headroom: dynamic-range-limit holds thumbnails at standard brightness and lets a hero or a hovered badge go to no-limit. Gain-map images do the same thing for artwork, carrying an SDR picture plus the instructions to brighten it. The hover keeps a brightness-and-bloom fallback so the gesture still reads on an SDR screen.
drops.source: Chris Bennett — SoVeryBright (HDR gain-map logo exports)

interaction.mouse: Hover a badge to hand it the headroom; the pointer also drags a light pool across the stage.
interaction.click: Pick which limit the hover applies and dial the SDR bloom up or down.
interaction.touch: Tap a badge for the same transition; the support readout says what this screen can actually do.

drops.title: The Host That Reads Its Slots
drops.description: No variant attribute — the card inspects what was slotted into it, and restyles its own shell to match.
drops.concept: :host(:has(…)) lets a shadow host react to the light DOM it was handed, and Safari 27 adds :host:has(…), which looks inside the shadow tree the component built for itself. Slot a picture and the card goes two-column; slot a badge and the accent rail lights; leave the body out and it collapses to a compact row — all configuration-free. The demo writes both selector forms as separate rules and reports which one this engine honours.

interaction.mouse: Toggle badge, media, footer and body copy and watch three cards relayout from content alone.
interaction.click: The shadow-alert and outline switches show the shadow-tree form of the selector firing.
interaction.touch: Checkbox panel sits inline on narrow screens; the code readout updates with every change.
